chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Moten as a pianist and the 1929 versus 1932 recordings
summary: Moten read anything and played well only with music in front of him; the 1932 sides began to swing more.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Benny Morton himself, how good a reader was he?
Had an awful piano player. That's like -- Fats Waller, he was something. Read anything he see, show me, bird's eyes --
But he never sounds wonderful on the records, does he?
No, only when the music's there. Only when the music's there.
No, he could play the music if you showed it to him.
I see. But the thing is, the difference between those records of 1929 and those of '32 is very considerable, because his band doesn't swing very much at all. Not as a band, you know.
They started some swinging with that Morton Swing stuff. Might have been the rhythm section, they had a lot of changes they had to do.
